title: Hollywood westerns
text: In the 1940s and 1950s, Hollywood crews came to the rugged country around Gallup to shoot westerns on location. Films made there include Pursued, Four Faces West, and Escape from Fort Bravo. Crews and stars used Gallup's El Rancho Hotel as their base, encouraged by its owner, R. E. Griffith, and his brother, the director D. W. Griffith. By 1964, the lure of the western hero was fading.

s2.title: Film Office
s2.quote: The rugged terrain surrounding Gallup was popular with Hollywood filmmakers during the 1940s and 50s for the on-location shooting of Westerns. ... Films made in Gallup include Billy the Kid (1930), Pursued (1947), The Sea of Grass (1947), Four Faces West (1948), Only the Valiant (1951), Ace in the Hole (1951), Escape from Fort Bravo (1953)

s3.title: New Mexico: El Rancho Hotel
s3.quote: Joe Massaglia constructed the El Rancho Hotel in 1936 along U.S. Route 66 for Mr. R.E. “Griff” Griffith, brother of the famous movie director D.W. Griffith. ... Both Griff and his brother encouraged moviemakers to use El Rancho as a base for crews and stars on location ... By 1964, however, the lure of the western hero was fading
